recommendation: Resolve all three findings and re-review exact revised bytes before WBS build.

findings.claim: The post-charge invalid-write recovery is contradictory and has no closed P3 entry: Section 5.2 permits POST_CHARGE_REPAIR_REQUIRED after persisted equality or strict-validation failure, while Section 9.1 assigns the same failed-validation or divergent-current condition to TRANSITION_RECOVERY_BLOCKED_DIVERGENT with DIVERGENT_CURRENT_TERMINAL_RECOVERY as its sole exit; the original intent and OPEN index entry remain unresolved, so the ordinary zero-open-intent prerequisite also prevents a separate repair intent.

locator.value: 5.2 Commit semantics step 7; 9.1 Freeze rule incomplete-intent recovery

findings.disposition_reason: Confirmed invalid-write recovery has conflicting states and unresolved OPEN lineage.

findings.claim: The charge-boundary evidence order cannot satisfy its own binding rule: the single boundary receipt is emitted before the final intent and its required administrative/index effects, but the final writer must later bind the post-append RootControlJournal current hash into that boundary aggregate while Section 5.2 forbids a replacement boundary receipt.

locator.value: 5.2 Commit semantics steps 5-6; 6.3 Bootstrap governance and accounting

findings.disposition_reason: Confirmed boundary evidence construction cyclically mixes preliminary and later effects.

findings.claim: The transition protocol defines recovery only when a valid intent was fully published before the OPEN append; it provides no state or authorized recovery for a partial, differing, or unreadable create-once ExecutionTransitionIntent, even though P3 scans the canonical intent root and the object cannot be overwritten.

locator.value: 9.1 Freeze rule, ordered OPEN and corruption recovery

findings.disposition_reason: Confirmed corrupt intent publication lacks an authorized pre-charge recovery.

residual_risks: Transition recovery and boundary evidence ordering remain incomplete.
